description: A day-cadence sub whose 24h window has fully elapsed is due; the next window is measured in seconds.
Only ~13.9h since the last pull: a correct seconds-based window holds the charge (the ×3600 bug would fire early).
The sub is past its expiresAtTs, so it is never pulled even though its period window is open.
An inactive (cancelled) subscription is never pulled.
expiresAtTs of 0 means no expiry, so the decision falls through to the seconds-based window (here, too early).
At exactly lastChargedTs + period the window is open and the pull fires.
A sub whose expiresAtTs is still in the future is not expired: a non-zero expiry alone must never hold a charge.
At exactly expiresAtTs the subscription has lapsed: the last chargeable second is expiresAtTs - 1.
A sub that was cancelled AND has since lapsed reports 'canceled': a canceled subscription's expiry is meaningless, so the cancellation check runs first.
Chain time reading BEFORE the last successful pull (clock skew, or a crank replaying an old slot) is too early, never due: the window is a direction, not a distance.
